items.title: Show HN: Unofficial 3DS Port of F-Zero X Written by Claude Code
items.why_it_matters: A developer successfully ported the classic game F-Zero X to the Nintendo 3DS at 60fps using Claude Code, sharing a detailed postmortem on how they guided the AI through a massive codebase. As a vibe coder, this is real-world proof of how far you can push Claude Code when you focus on directing rather than typing. This week, read their postmortem and apply their strategy of breaking large files into smaller, AI-readable modules on your AI-ingest project.

items.title: Show HN: Gage – Rust based tool to scan Claude sessions for bugs, other issues
items.why_it_matters: Gage is a new open-source CLI tool that scans your Claude Code session transcripts to find bugs you might have blindly approved during fast-paced coding sessions. Since you rely on AI to write most of your code, this acts as an automated safety net for things you missed in the git diff. This week, install Gage via your terminal and run it against your AI-ingest repo to see if Claude snuck any bugs past you.

items.title: Portal by Spotify cut my Claude Code token usage by 90%
items.why_it_matters: Spotify released Portal, an internal utility that optimizes how context is sent to Claude Code, resulting in a 90% reduction in token usage. For a developer building apps with Claude Code, this directly translates to faster response times and significantly lower API costs. This week, check out the Portal repository and integrate their context-pruning configuration into your local Claude Code setup.

items.title: Show HN: DeepMem plugin for Claude Code – persistent semantic memory via MCP
items.why_it_matters: DeepMem is a new Model Context Protocol (MCP) plugin for Claude Code that gives the AI persistent semantic memory across different terminal sessions. Instead of constantly re-explaining your Next.js and Supabase setup every time you start a new terminal, Claude can now remember your project's architecture automatically. This week, install the DeepMem MCP plugin and run a test session to see if Claude remembers your database schema without being prompted.

items.title: Tell HN: Check your Claude settings, it may have silently enabled remote access
items.why_it_matters: A bug in a recent Claude Code release (v2.1.257) may have silently enabled the Remote Control (/rc) feature on your local machine without your explicit consent. Since you use Claude Code daily, this is a critical security setting to verify to ensure your terminal isn't exposed. This week, run `claude config` in your terminal to check your remote control status and update to the latest version to patch the bug.
